extension.displayName: DataNest – Database Client for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server, MongoDB, Redis
extension.description: Free open-source database client and SQL editor for MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, ClickHouse, MongoDB, Redis and Elasticsearch: table designer, ER diagram, import and export, no account, no telemetry.

configuration.completion.enabled.descrip: Offer DataNest's own SQL completion (keywords, tables, columns) while typing. Turn it off to keep the editor's quick suggestions and other completion providers only; the editor's `editor.quickSuggestions` setting is not touched.
configuration.tree.dragNames.description: Dragging a database, schema, table, view or column from the tree into a text editor types its name, quoted for that database. Turn it off to drag only inside the tree.
configuration.pageSize.description: Rows shown on one page when a table is opened from the tree.
configuration.results.rowHeight.descript: How tall the rows of the result grid are. A button in the grid's toolbar changes it for you alone, and that choice wins over this setting.
configuration.results.rowHeight.compact: Compact: 24 px, more rows on screen.
configuration.results.rowHeight.comforta: Comfortable: 40 px, more air around the text.
configuration.results.maxColumnWidth.des: The widest a column of the result grid gets on its own, in pixels (120–1600). Dragging a separator still makes it wider, and Fit to Content may go beyond it up to 800 px.
configuration.results.restore.descriptio: Bring back the result tabs of a saved SQL file after the editor restarts. Only the statement and its connection are kept, never rows or passwords, and only statements that merely read. A restored tab is empty until you click Run.
configuration.results.restoreRun.descrip: Run the restored tabs again on their own after a restart. Only statements that merely read, and never on a production or switched-off connection. Off by default: a restored tab waits for you to click Run.

configuration.queryTimeout.description: Seconds a statement may run before DataNest cancels it. `0` means no limit.

configuration.historyLimit.description: Number of executed statements kept in the query history. `0` turns the history off. Passwords in `IDENTIFIED BY '...'`, `password = ...` and similar are masked before saving.
configuration.safeMode.description: What DataNest does before running a `DELETE` or `UPDATE` without `WHERE`, `DROP` or `TRUNCATE`.

configuration.queryVariables.description: What `:name`, `${name}` and positional placeholders (`?` in MySQL and SQLite, `$1` in PostgreSQL, `:1` in Oracle) in a statement do. DataNest asks for each value before the statement runs and puts it in as a literal: a number, `NULL` or text (in single quotes, `'42'` stays text). Strings, comments and routine or trigger definitions are left alone.
configuration.queryVariables.remember: Ask, offering the value given last time
configuration.queryVariables.ask: Ask every time; nothing is kept
configuration.queryVariables.off: Leave them in the text as written
configuration.editor.codeLens.descriptio: Show **▶ Run** above each statement of a SQL editor.
Highlight the statement under the cursor — the one `Ctrl+Enter` runs — when a SQL file holds several. The colour is `datanest.statementHighlightBackground` in `workbench.colorCustomizations`.
configuration.editor.foldStatements.desc: Fold SQL by statements, as well as by block comments, `-- #region` markers and indentation. Off: the editor's own folding by indentation.
color.statementHighlightBackground: Background of the statement under the cursor in a SQL editor.
configuration.tree.expandOnlyByArrow.des: A table in the tree opens and closes only by its arrow; a double click on its name opens its data and leaves the row as it was. The editor toggles a row on a double click by itself and offers no way to switch that off for one view, so DataNest puts the row back at once (one blink at most). Turn it off to keep the editor's own behaviour.
configuration.tree.showSizes.description: Show the size of a database or schema after its name (`public 2.4M`). It is read lazily with one small query and never blocks the tree. The server version after a connection (`15.19 · user@host:5432`) is always shown, and kept for the next start, so it is there before you connect.
configuration.tree.tableStats.descriptio: Show the estimated rows of each table in the tree, and its size and comment in the tooltip — from the server's own statistics, never a `COUNT(*)`. SQLite keeps no such statistics.

configuration.connections.sync.descripti: Share your connection list (with its folders and settings) between your computers through the editor's **Settings Sync**. Passwords never travel: each computer keeps its own in its secret storage, so type them once on each. Paths to SQLite files and SSH keys must exist on each computer.
